title: Cyclotomic Obstructions and Optimal Truncation for the Herglotz--Zagier Function
scope: Targeted continuation of the Herglotz--Zagier thread in Analysis/Polylogarithms/docs; not a complete audit of every source formula.

status_conventions.proved_in_article: A mathematical proof is supplied in the manuscript, with the stated classical inputs.
status_conventions.known_input: Prior literature or standard mathematics used by the continuation, not claimed as a new result.
status_conventions.supporting_computation: Finite exact verification, symbolic computation, numerical evidence, or rational certificates; does not replace the general proof.
status_conventions.formal: In the rational pre-Bloch/five-term calculus, with logarithmic products and pi^2 permitted in analytic realizations. Negative formal results are not numerical transcendence assertions.

results.statement: For q>=3 and G_q=(Z/qZ)^*/{+/-1}, every rational relation among beta_q(a) has coefficients c_a=c_(a^-1), and all such coefficient vectors are relations.
consequences: beta_q(a)=0 if and only if a^2 is congruent to +1 or -1 modulo q
results.limits: The proof is an algebraic exterior-symbol theorem; no period-injectivity or transcendence assumption is used.

results.statement: For q>2 the rank is (phi(q)-r_plus(q)-r_minus(q))/4. The complete list of conductors with identically zero beta is {1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12,24}.
results.limits: The zero-conductor list alone is not a denominator-only reduction criterion for F(p/q).

results.statement: For coprime p,q, beta_q(p)-beta_p(q) lies in the rational exterior square if and only if both beta symbols vanish.
results.limits: The proof applies the exterior square of the normalized norm on the multiplicative vector space, not the average Galois action on its exterior square.

results.statement: For reduced positive p/q, formal rational-dilogarithm reduction holds if and only if p^2==+/-1 mod q and q^2==+/-1 mod p, with independently chosen signs. Formal pure-logarithm reduction holds if and only if min(p,q)=1.
results.limits: The successful cases yield numerical identities. The unsuccessful cases exclude five-term certificates, not every conceivable numerical relation.

results.statement: Up to reciprocal interchange, all admissible coprime pairs occur as adjacent terms in the three recurrence families described in the article: the minus recurrence with parameter K>=2, the plus recurrence with parameter K>=1, and consecutive odd-index Fibonacci numbers.
results.proof_method: Vieta descent preserving coprimality and swapping the two square signs; invariant integer recurrence parameters.
results.limits: Families can overlap at small pairs; the finite enumeration is supplementary to the proof of completeness.

results.statement: Every successful formal reduction has a constructible rational dilogarithm core with arguments in (0,1), an exact exterior boundary certificate, and O(log max(p,q)) terms after the consecutive-pair shortcut.
results.limits: The algorithm does not compute the remaining logarithmic products. Optional trial factorization used in diagnostic prime-coordinate checks is not assigned a polynomial bit-complexity bound.

results.statement: For q>=2, J(2/q) is formally pure-logarithmic exactly for q in {2,3,5} or 4|q. It is formally reducible to rational dilogarithms exactly for q in {2,3,5,6,10} or 4|q.
results.limits: All positive cases have explicit analytic evaluations. Necessity is in the formal calculus. The q=1 value is separately elementary.

results.statement: Explicit formulas cover all positive formal J cases, including J(1/3), J(1/5), and the infinite even-m family J(1/m)=pi^2(m^2-2)/(48m)+S(m)-S(m/2)/2-S(2m)/2.
results.limits: The direct-integral verification is high-precision floating point, not a rigorous quadrature enclosure.

results.statement: For a=2*pi*x and bounded delta=N-pi*x, the positive truncation error has leading factor x^(-1/2)*exp(-2*pi*x), explicit rational-polynomial corrections C_j(delta), and a uniform expansion on each fixed bounded delta interval.
results.limits: The real uniformity regime is specified in the article; no unrestricted complex-sector version is asserted.

results.statement: Consecutive truncation errors have unique positive crossovers, yielding an exact description of the optimal integer cutoff. The first correction to the minimum depends periodically on dist(pi*x-1/4,Z).
results.limits: A nearest-integer leading approximation does not replace the exact transition sequence close to a crossover.

results.statement: Relative to the exactly defined one-frequency transition, the full transition with K=2N+2 has leading arithmetic displacement -(9/10)*K*2^(-K), with the further error terms given in the article.
results.limits: An exactly defined reference is essential: an algebraically truncated reference would obscure this exponentially smaller displacement.

results.statement: Positive-measure moment inequalities bound the truncation remainder and give rigorous rational enclosures when the moments are enclosed by exact Euler--Maclaurin bounds.
results.limits: The supplied interval examples concern F(2), F(4), F(8), and F(16). They are distinct from the floating-point transition checks.

results.statement: At q=7,n=2, the untwisted finite-field three-term expression printed in the inspected preprint has exact defect 3*beta_7(2), which is nonzero.
results.source_scope: Radchenko--Zagier arXiv:2012.15805v1, Section 7.2, page 16 of the inspected 18-page preprint.
results.limits: No automatic assertion is made about the separate uninspected journal text or the distinct rational-variable cocycle.

known_inputs.statement: The finite cyclotomic dilogarithm representation of F(p/q)-F(1), its Galois invariance, and its beta boundary formula originate in Radchenko--Zagier. The boundary is also checked directly in the continuation.
F inversion and three-term relations, the relation between J and F, reciprocal-integer evaluations, and several worked rational evaluations are prior inputs.
The Binet--Lambert positive integral representation is prior work. The new analytic contribution is its sharp truncation analysis and the explicit effective consequences.
The Fourier coefficient of the primitive cyclotomic logarithm profile is a nonzero Gauss sum times L(1,conjugate chi), up to its stated normalization.
A nonprincipal Dirichlet L-function has nonzero value at 1. This classical theorem, not a numerical determinant estimate, supplies the Gram-matrix nonvanishing.
Rational Galois descent for Bloch groups, the vanishing B(Q) tensor Q=0, and torsion of K2^M(Q) are standard algebraic inputs already used in RZ Section 7.2.
The reduction of all rational derivatives to cyclotomic polylogarithms of bounded weight is already stated immediately after RZ Proposition 4; this package does not claim it as new.

open_questions.question: Can a numerical reduction exist when the corresponding formal exterior obstruction is nonzero? The package supplies no period-injectivity or transcendence theorem.
Construct a practical, branch-controlled algorithm for the complete logarithmic remainder accompanying every successful rational core.
Develop additional exponentially small arithmetic sectors and their interactions beyond the explicitly proved transition displacement.
Extend the real optimal-truncation analysis to suitably specified complex sectors and Stokes transitions.
Formalize the exact group, norm, recurrence, and interval-certificate arguments in a proof assistant.
Supply the missing class-group, class-number, and unit-index arguments before promoting the fitted Stark/regulator tables in the earlier drafts to unconditional general formulas.
